clue.text: Ways to nab a very loud number of crooks?

indicators.note: to nab is to seize and hold, so the first piece grips the others inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way; two of them make the plural
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how to catch a big, noisy gang of criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooks' suggests criminals, but here it means shepherds' crooks, the hooked sticks, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A shepherd's crook is a kind of walking stick, so several crooks are a number of staffs.

clue.text: Commercial mail centre undergoing renovation

indicators.note: something being renovated is pulled apart and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A business sorting office is being refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercantile describes trade and merchants, the same sphere as commercial activity.

clue.text: Resounding section of the chorus

definitions.note: read as a noun, a resounding sound

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from a whole, so the letters lie within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Describing a part of the choir's singing that rings out loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resounding' must be read as a noun, the act of sounding again, to swap for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is sound reflected back, a re-sounding of the original noise.

clue.text: Bluff bordering some deep chasm

indicators.note: a border runs around the edge, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: to bluff is to con, to deceive
some and any are interchangeable determiners

explanation.surface: A cliff edge running alongside a great ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' looks like a cliff in a landscape scene, but it is a verb meaning deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep gorge, which is a chasm cut by a river.

clue.text: Area regularly guarded by mean, threatening fish

indicators.note: something guarded is surrounded by its protector, so it goes inside
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: A dangerous fish patrols its territory, protected by something nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray carries a venomous barbed tail, so it is a fish that can threaten.

clue.text: Voyager coming upon river on top edge of rainforest

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
the Ure is a Yorkshire river

indicators.note: the top edge of a word in a down light is its first letter

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives at a river near the jungle's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'upon' and 'on' place each piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer is someone who travels in search of exploits, a voyager into the unknown.

clue.text: Entitled chap jumping the gun endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: to jump the gun is to act too early

explanation.surface: A self-important man keeps starting things too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entitled' suggests arrogance, but it means holding a title.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a nobleman holding a hereditary title, so a titled man.

clue.text: Magazine produced by group in class

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: a caste is a social class

explanation.surface: A school magazine put together by a team of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: A magazine here is a cartridge holding tape or film, not a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a sealed case of tape, much as a magazine holds film or ammunition.

clue.text: Forthright Republican interrupting troublemakers at the front entrance

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this letter is placed inside the rest
the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
as a verb, to entrance is to enchant

explanation.surface: An outspoken politician breaks into a row of rowdy protesters at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway, but it is the verb meaning bewitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant comment is incisive and direct, the manner of someone forthright.

clue.text: Short American soap opera?

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A brief US television serial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a short drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is one example of television drama, hence the question mark.

clue.text: After toiling here one might check out, cause unknown

definitions.text: After toiling here one might check out

parts.note: a factor is a contributing cause

explanation.surface: Someone leaves after hard labour for some mysterious reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check out' suggests a hotel; here it is clocking off at the end of a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory is a works where labourers toil and clock out when their shift ends.

clue.text: Mostly unnecessary feature of record players

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A largely pointless part of a gramophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A record player's stylus is called a needle, the point that reads the groove.

clue.text: Love to abandon healthy person having cocktail?

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving, so that letter departs from what follows

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like O
an owner is someone who has something

explanation.surface: A romance ends when a fit person takes to mixed drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The O leaves SOUND, not OWNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset; a cocktail is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Nothing provided by one hostel, strangely, is free

indicators.note: strangely suggests something oddly arranged, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Odd that one particular youth hostel offers no charge for anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' reads like no charge, but it means at liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaped animal or fugitive on the loose is at large, unconfined and so free.

clue.text: Drunk unwilling to pay for a round?

definitions.text: unwilling to pay for a round?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: stingy, avoiding buying drinks

explanation.surface: An inebriated drinker who dodges buying everyone's drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang both for intoxicated and for miserly, as in tight with money.

clue.text: Vulnerable creature adapting to change without a companion in the end

indicators.note: change says the letters are to be altered into a fresh order
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: An endangered animal struggles to adjust to a new life alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means with these letters added outside, all thrown into the mix. 'Vulnerable' is the official conservation status of the species.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List, so it is a vulnerable creature.

clue.text: Urban bar about to introduce starters of unbelievably immense loaded tacos

indicators.note: introducing brings something in, so the letters go inside
about means turned around, so the word is read in the other direction
starters are the openings, so the first letter of each word is kept

explanation.surface: A city bar serves astonishingly large, heavily filled tacos.
explanation.definitionFit: A built-up area is densely covered with buildings, as cities are, so it means urban.

clue.text: Gang endeavour to support current illegal activity

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A gang strives to back current lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'to support' sets the endeavour piece beneath the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery by bandits, a form of lawless criminal behaviour.

clue.text: Skin from potatoes covering more second-rate veggies

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the outer letters enclose the rest
a skin is the outer layer, so only the outside letters are kept

explanation.surface: Potato peel wrapped round further inferior vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Potherbs are leafy plants cooked as greens, so a kind of vegetable.

clue.text: Distance, say, a cart reversed

indicators.note: reversed means turned back to front, so the whole string is read the other way

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say
a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: How far a cart has backed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance measured in yards, as in sports like golf or American football.

clue.text: Energy encapsulated by lovely flower girl, perhaps?

indicators.note: a capsule surrounds its contents, so this letter is held inside

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A pretty bridesmaid full of vigour at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'flower girl, perhaps?', not 'lovely flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's young niece is a typical choice as the flower girl at a wedding, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Alerted to crashing bore

indicators.note: something crashing is smashed up, so its letters end up in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is warned that a dull person is about to gatecrash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person, but it is the past tense of bear, to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to endure it, so bore is the past tense meaning put up with.

clue.text: Big cat grabbing a deer's tail and part of throat

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the first word encloses the rest

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

indicators.note: a tail is the hind end, so the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: A wild cat seizes a deer by the rump and then the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx is the voice box, the organ at the top of the windpipe in the throat.

clue.text: Formal doctor gets a say occasionally

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A stiff physician is sometimes allowed to have their say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the alternating run.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are smart and elegant, suited to a formal occasion.

clue.text: Better type of comedy movie finally

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word before it, its last letter

explanation.surface: A superior comic film at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning make better.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to make it superior, which is to improve it.

clue.text: What may be felt in one's stomach after eating too much French bread?

definitions.text: What may be felt in one's stomach after eating too much

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French word for bread

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence about overeating baguettes; it splits into an English word and a French one with the same spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeating brings stomach ache, and the same four letters are the word for bread in French.

clue.text: Grind last bit of pepper — a pinch!

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, a trace

explanation.surface: A cook mills the last of the pepper and adds just a pinch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grind' looks like milling pepper; it is the noun for daily drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the exhausting competitive routine of working life, the daily grind.

clue.text: Time away from work is dandy!

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone declares a holiday from the job splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy' looks like the old adjective for excellent, but it is the noun for a smart dresser; a toff is a posh, well-dressed person.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is a stylish upper-class man, much like a dandy who prizes fine clothes.

clue.text: Means of checking rules, we're told

indicators.note: being told something is hearing it spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: A way of verifying regulations, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checking' looks like inspecting, but it means restraining.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are straps used to hold back a horse, a means of restraint.

clue.text: Good faith in sofa bed misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced things are put in the wrong positions, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Trust in a fold-out bed is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fides is Latin for good faith, used for honest intention or genuine credentials.
